cards.title: Accops HyID: Identity and Access Management Datasheet (V5, 2026)
cards.key_problem: Enterprises need one identity layer that covers Windows and Linux logins, legacy applications, network equipment and SaaS at once, rather than a cloud IAM product that only reaches modern SAML applications.
key_outcomes: MFA for Windows and Linux desktop, server, RDP and SSH login
Face authentication for Windows desktop login via Credential Provider
Offline login using mobile apps or hardware tokens
REST API adds MFA to any custom application
Contextual risk scoring drives silent or step-up authentication
cards.brief: The current HyID datasheet and the newest identity document in the library. HyID is positioned as a cloud-native IdP covering authentication, authorisation and audit across both modern and legacy estates: Windows and Linux logins, RDP and SSH, web and legacy applications, remote-access gateways, firewalls and switches over RADIUS, and SAML applications such as Office 365 and Salesforce. Authentication methods span OTP over SMS, email, software and hardware tokens, FIDO2 and U2F security keys, push notifications, QR codes, and fingerprint and face biometrics. Access risk is scored from location, device posture, browser, time and behaviour, so low-risk sessions authenticate silently and risky ones step up. Deployable on-premises, in a customer VPC, Accops-managed, or hybrid.
cards.use_for: Any MFA, SSO or IAM requirement, and specifically where the prospect needs MFA on legacy applications or desktop logins that a SaaS-only IAM product cannot reach.
cards.internal_reason: No public URL confirmed for this edition. Product literature with no customer detail, so it is a candidate for publication - Siddharth approves.
cards.compliance_note: Names DPDP, GDPR, HIPAA, PCI DSS, SOX, NIST and ISO 27001 as supported compliance frameworks. Useful for procurement questionnaires alongside the ISO certificate.

cards.title: Accops HySecure Gateway: Remote Access and Security Gateway Datasheet (V3)
cards.key_problem: A remote-access gateway has to cover every application type, every client platform and every deployment model at once, and most products cover only the web-application slice of that.
key_outcomes: TLS 1.3 with quantum-safe encryption algorithms listed
Device identification on over 20 parameters including CPUID, MBID, HDDID, MACID, IMEI
Access modes: HyLite HTML5 clientless, agent, full client, mobile, L3 VPN, reverse proxy
Active-Active N+1 cluster, scalable to thousands of users
Runs on VMware, XenServer, Hyper-V, AWS, Azure, OCI, GCP, Nutanix and Kubernetes
cards.brief: The full HySecure Gateway specification: application support, access security, management, authentication, auditing, authorisation, endpoint control, access modes and deployment. Application coverage runs past web to TCP and UDP client-server applications, Windows file shares, dynamic-port applications, RDP virtual channels, published subnets, VDI through HyWorks, and SaaS including Microsoft 365 and Salesforce. Endpoint control identifies devices on more than twenty hardware parameters, checks antivirus, firewall and Windows update state, and enforces geo-fencing plus clipboard, print and USB restriction. Deployment is deliberately broad - hardened Linux on any hardware, every major hypervisor and cloud, and a Kubernetes option.
cards.use_for: A technical evaluation or RFP response where the prospect wants the full capability list rather than a positioning pitch.

cards.title: Accops DaaS: Managed Cloud Desktops Brochure (2025)
cards.key_problem: Running VDI in-house means owning the provisioning, the refresh cycle and the integration of separate VDI, ZTNA and MFA products, which is capital expenditure and operational load a subscription can remove.
key_outcomes: Unifies ZTNA, MFA, VDI brokering, data protection and UX monitoring on one platform
Named in the Gartner Magic Quadrant
Zero-CapEx, pay-as-you-go consumption pricing
Two models: multi-tenant standardised catalogues, or a dedicated control plane
Runs on Azure including Jio Azure regions, AWS, OCI, and on-premise hypervisors
cards.brief: The 2025 DaaS brochure. Positions Accops DaaS as a managed, subscription cloud desktop platform whose differentiator is that ZTNA, MFA, VDI brokering, data protection and UX monitoring are one platform rather than integrated products. Two deployment models are offered: a multi-tenant control plane with Accops-managed standardised catalogues, or a dedicated control plane the customer controls and customises. Supported platforms include Azure with Jio Azure regions called out, AWS, OCI, and on-premise Hyper-V, ESXi, Nutanix AHV, Proxmox and OpenStack. Data-loss controls cover screenshot and screen-share blocking, directional upload, download and clipboard rules, watermarks, kiosk mode and session recording.
cards.use_for: A prospect who wants virtual desktops without buying and running the infrastructure, or one moving from CapEx to OpEx.

cards.title: Accops Digital Workspace: The Integrated Platform Brochure (2025)
cards.key_problem: Delivering secure work-from-anywhere normally means buying VDI, a remote-access gateway, MFA, SSO and thin clients from different vendors and making them work together.
key_outcomes: VDI, ZTNA gateway, IAM and thin clients as one integrated suite
SPAN technology for remote access over slow, high-latency networks
Endpoint trust evaluated before access, with location-based policy
Secure sandbox controlling clipboard, printing, USB, recording and internet
Modular - sized for businesses of any scale
cards.brief: The umbrella brochure for the whole platform, and the right first document when a prospect does not yet know which product they need. It sets out the four pillars - desktop and application virtualisation, a zero-trust application access gateway, identity and access management, and thin-client endpoints - and argues the integration case: one vendor instead of juggling product points. Remote access uses Accops' SPAN technology, aimed at slow and high-latency links. Endpoint trust is scanned and scored before access is granted, and policy can vary by device location. The secure sandbox is the data-protection story, controlling clipboard, printing, session recording, file saving, USB and internet access.
cards.use_for: First meeting with a prospect who has not scoped a specific product, or an executive audience who needs the platform story rather than a feature list.

cards.title: Accops HyDesk: Eco-Smart Thin and Zero Client Endpoints Brochure (V5)
cards.key_problem: A PC estate carries the cost of energy, refresh cycles, patching and per-desk support, and none of that is addressed by virtualising the desktop if the endpoint is still a full PC.
key_outcomes: Up to 80% lower power consumption than a PC
Hardware certified for a 7-year service life, extending refresh cycles
Three tiers: zero client, standard thin PC, power-user thin PC
Works with Microsoft RDS, VMware Horizon, Citrix Workspace and Accops
HyAssist gives cross-NAT remote control without firewall or proxy changes
cards.brief: The endpoint hardware story. HyDesk is a family of thin and zero clients in three tiers - a zero client for pure VDI, a standard thin PC that also runs a local browser and LibreOffice, and a power-user thin PC supporting Windows Embedded and SSDs. Three operating modes cover kiosk, local desktop and Windows Embedded. The commercial argument is energy and lifecycle: up to 80% less power, certified for seven years, with centralised deployment, patching, auditing and remote troubleshooting through a single console. Notably vendor-neutral on the back end - it lists Microsoft RDS, VMware Horizon and Citrix Workspace alongside Accops Digital Workspace.
cards.use_for: An endpoint refresh or green-IT conversation, and any VDI deal where the customer has not decided what sits on the desk. The vendor-neutral compatibility makes it usable even where the VDI stack is a competitor's.

cards.title: Accops Nano OS: BYOD Access from a USB Stick Brochure (V4)
cards.key_problem: Giving contractors and BYOD users secure access normally means shipping, managing and recovering corporate laptops, and the personal device underneath may already carry a keylogger or malware.
key_outcomes: Boots any personal PC into a read-only hardened Linux Live OS from USB
Bypasses any keylogger or malware resident on the host device
All session data wiped at reboot, no trace on the personal device
Blocks host storage, clipboard, USB, printing and screen capture
Runs on any USB 3.0 drive of 4 GB or more
cards.brief: Nano is an AES-256 encrypted, customised Ubuntu LTS Live OS delivered on a USB stick. Booting a personal device from it produces a clean, read-only environment that a keylogger or malware on the host cannot reach, and which leaves nothing behind at reboot. Access to private applications runs through HySecure, and to virtual desktops through Accops Digital Workspace, with single sign-on, MFA and contextual checks at boot. Policy enforcement covers applications, internet and devices per user, role or group, with clipboard, USB, printing and screen-capture lockdown plus full audit trails. The commercial argument is avoiding the cost and logistics of corporate laptops entirely.
cards.use_for: Contractor, vendor or BYOD access where shipping laptops is impractical, and regulated environments that need no data residue on a personal device.

cards.title: Accops Digital Workspace on Proxmox: Open-Source Virtualisation for VDI (V2, Oct 2025)
cards.key_problem: The hypervisor licence is often the largest line in a VDI budget, and most VDI products tie the customer to a proprietary hypervisor whose pricing they do not control.
key_outcomes: Runs Accops Digital Workspace on Proxmox, a licence-free open-source hypervisor
Full and linked cloning, snapshots, load balancing and high availability
Storage across NFS, Ceph, ZFS, iSCSI and local
Comparison table against VMware Horizon and Citrix on cost and complexity
Positioned for SMB and mid-sized deployments, scalable upward
cards.brief: The open-source hypervisor option, and the direct commercial answer to Broadcom's VMware pricing. Accops Digital Workspace runs on Proxmox, removing the hypervisor licence from the VDI budget entirely while keeping the HyWorks workflows for desktop reservation, pooling and session management unchanged. Features covered are full and linked cloning, snapshot-based restore with an explicit caveat that snapshots are short-term only, load balancing, high availability, a single web management console, asynchronous job handling for long-running clones, and storage across NFS, Ceph, ZFS, iSCSI and local. A comparison table sets it against VMware Horizon and Citrix on cost, deployment complexity and scalability, and is honest that Proxmox suits small to mid-sized deployments where the others are enterprise-scale.
cards.use_for: A cost-driven VDI deal, an SMB or mid-market prospect, or any customer reacting to VMware licensing changes who wants the hypervisor cost gone rather than reduced.
cards.internal_reason: No public URL confirmed. Candidate for publication - it names competitors only in a factual comparison table.

cards.title: Accops Virtual Browser: Remote Browser Isolation for Air-Gapped Environments
cards.key_problem: Government and defence sites give each user two physical PCs, one for internet and one air-gapped, and the internet PC still accumulates persistent malware, tracking cookies and APTs that conventional endpoint security does not detect.
key_outcomes: Browser runs in a container in the data centre; only encrypted pixels reach the endpoint
Endpoint state resets daily, so persistent malware and APTs are wiped
Removes the second physical PC per desk
Blocks cookie-based user profiling and session or browser takeover
Removes civil broadband landing inside critical sites
cards.brief: A technical product document rather than a brochure, written for government and defence. It starts from the two-device architecture those sites actually run - a separate internet PC and an air-gapped intranet PC per desk, with USB-based manual transfer and data diodes - and enumerates what that model still fails to stop: undetected persistent malware on the internet PC, cookie-based user profiling that enables targeted attacks, data exfiltration, session and browser takeover through malicious plug-ins, and civil broadband lines terminating inside critical sites. Remote Browser Isolation is the proposed answer: execute all web code in a containerised browser in a secure data centre and stream only encrypted visual content, so the endpoint stays stateless and resets to a clean state daily.
cards.use_for: Government, defence and any air-gapped or high-security environment where users need internet access. The strongest asset for the two-PCs-per-desk cost argument.
cards.internal_reason: Describes the security architecture of government and defence customers in detail. Not for general distribution.

cards.title: Accops Huddle: Remote Support and Diagnostics for Government IT Helpdesks (V3)
cards.client: A leading Indian government agency, quoted anonymously by a scientist
cards.key_problem: Government IT helpdesks supporting isolated networks cannot use TeamViewer, AnyDesk or any internet-based remote-support tool, and often have no compliant alternative for Linux and Bharat OS desktops.
key_outcomes: Make in India product compliant with Government of India statutory guidelines
Runs fully on-premise in isolated networks with no internet dependency
Supports Windows, Ubuntu, CentOS and Bharat OS
TLS-encrypted desktop sharing, file transfer, chat and multi-party sessions
Full session and participant audit logs including camera, mic and screen-share events
cards.brief: A remote diagnostics and support tool built for government helpdesks, and explicitly the replacement for TeamViewer, AnyDesk and Webex in environments where those cannot be used. It runs on-premise inside isolated networks without needing internet access, and can also extend over the internet or cloud where that is permitted. Features cover on-demand and scheduled meetings, desktop control, multi-party sessions, file sharing and chat, bandwidth optimisation for low-bandwidth and rural sites, role-based access, MFA including biometric and passwordless, AD and SSO integration, workgroup accounts for sites without AD, branding customisation, and detailed session and participant audit logs. Cross-platform support includes Bharat OS, with macOS planned. Carries an anonymous customer quote from a scientist at a leading government agency.
cards.use_for: A government or public-sector helpdesk requirement, an isolated-network support problem, or any deal where a Make in India product is a procurement requirement.
